Let me analyze this conflict.

The register says: "R049/2006-NL1-2012.03"
The document says: "R49-1/2006-NL1-12.03"

These are two formats of the same OIML certificate number. Let me decompose:

Register: R049 / 2006 - NL1 - 2012.03
Document: R49-1 / 2006 - NL1 - 12.03

OIML certificate numbering convention: The certificate number typically follows the pattern of the recommendation (R49, which is for continuous totalizing systems... actually R49 is water meters for cold potable water — Part 1: Metrological requirements — R49-1/2006), country code (NL1 = Netherlands NMi Certin), year (2012), and sequence number (03).

Document: "R49-1/2006-NL1-12.03" — R49-1/2006 is the OIML recommendation R49-1 edition 2006, NL1 is the issuing authority, 12.03 = year 12 (2012), certificate number 03.

Register: "R049/2006-NL1-2012.03" — R049 is the recommendation with leading zero, 2012.03 = full year 2012, sequence 03.

Also, the register id is 3088, and the embedded comments show cert_id: 3088 and num: R049/2006-NL1-2012.03 — so the register form is the canonical database form. The source PDF filename is r049-2006-nl1-2012-03.pdf, matching the register form.

This clearly denotes the same certificate. Per the rules: "Number/year format differences that clearly denote the same certificate = same-entity with the register's canonical form."

So verdict: same-entity, best_value: "R049/2006-NL1-2012.03" (register form).

Why: Both formats decompose to recommendation R49(-1)/2006, issuing authority NL1, year 2012 (12), sequence 03 — the document uses "12" for 2012 and "R49-1" vs "R049", same certificate; register canonical form per rules.

The output must be one JSON object with the axes array containing one axis entry (num).
